subject: SLA exception governance & monthly credit floor — CloudSail negotiation
messages:
From: Sarah Park <sarah@cloudsail.com>
To: markus_klein@redwood.ai
Cc: contracts@cloudsail.com
Date: 2026-08-28T09:12:00Z
Subject: CloudSail SLA template — initial ask and exceptions

Markus,

Thanks for the demo earlier this week — CloudSail’s team liked the predictable latency profiles. As we move toward procurement, our legal and ops teams have a couple of asks on the SLA template before we can sign: 

- We typically insist on a monthly credit floor so small outages don’t net zero credit in practice (our finance team needs a minimum remedy). Can you propose a floor amount tied to the monthly committed spend?
- For batched inference paths (our heavy jobs), we may need latency carveouts during scheduled model retrains — can that be an exception in the SLA rather than a fault event?
- We also want a governance process for temporary uplifts to the uptime target during onboarding (we can accept a phased ramp).

I’ve attached our standard ops runbook and highlighted sections for review. If you can sketch a proposal this week we can bring it to our procurement meeting next Tuesday.

Best,
Sarah
Sarah Park
Head of Platform Ops, CloudSail
attachments: ops-runbook.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: markus_klein@redwood.ai
To: Sarah Park <sarah@cloudsail.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-29T14:03:00Z
Subject: Re: CloudSail SLA template — initial ask and exceptions

Sarah —

Appreciate the clear list. Short answers up front, then a proposed approach: 

1) Monthly credit floor: we can offer a floor expressed as 2% of monthly committed spend (applies to hosted API only) as a minimum payout when an SLA breach qualifies. That prevents micro-payouts.

2) Batched inference carveouts: we can classify scheduled model retrains and planned batch windows as a documented "batch maintenance window" that is excluded from uptime calculations provided the window is pre-notified and < 8 hours/month.

3) Onboarding uplift: we are open to a 90-day ramp where uptime target moves from 99.90% to 99.95% after the first 30 days, contingent on usage patterns.

I’m attaching an annotated SLA draft (SLA_Draft_v3.pdf) that folds these items into the remedy and maintenance carveout sections. Ben, can you weigh in on whether the 2% floor is operationally reasonable for us? Laura, any redline flags from a contracting perspective?

Proposed next step: 1) Sarah to confirm CloudSail can accept 8h/month carveout for batch windows if pre-notified, 2) we send final redlines and a DocuSign link by end of week.

Thanks,
Markus
Markus Klein
VP Sales, Redwood Inference
attachments: SLA_Draft_v3.pdf (annotated)

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: markus_klein@redwood.ai, Sarah Park <sarah@cloudsail.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-30T09:27:00Z
Subject: Re: CloudSail SLA template — initial ask and exceptions

Quick note from ops/sales ops perspective: 

- 2% floor looks OK for deals of this size but we should make it tiered: 2% floor for monthly committed spend < $100k, 1.25% floor for $100k–$500k, and 0.75% for larger commitments. That lets us keep overall exposure bounded.
- For batch maintenance windows, request that CloudSail gives a rolling 72-hour notice for planned retrains so we can avoid unexpected capacity shifts that affect other customers.
- Also suggest we add a soft cap on monthly credits at 30% of monthly committed spend to avoid unlimited exposure on a sustained outage.

If CloudSail accepts the tiering + 72-hour notice, I think we can finalize.

Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: Sarah Park <sarah@cloudsail.com>, markus_klein@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-01T11:05:00Z
Subject: Re: CloudSail SLA template — initial ask and exceptions

Sarah / Markus —

From Legal: a few contracting points to close before DocuSign: 

- Please confirm the definition of "uptime" we use: we propose measured at the API route level (per-route p99 availability over calendar month) and not cluster-wide.
- The carveout for scheduled batch windows needs to be explicit: we want them to be listed as "pre-approved operational windows" in an annex so we can audit notices.
- For the credit floor tiering Ben proposed, we need to state the exact formula and examples in the SOW to prevent dispute (include illustrative examples for <$50k, $150k, and $600k spend bands).
- If CloudSail requires an onboarding uplift schedule, we ask to limit it to a single 90-day ramp per environment to prevent perpetual exceptions.

If you can confirm these items, we’ll incorporate redlines and issue a final agreement draft.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Sarah Park <sarah@cloudsail.com>
To: markus_klein@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: contracts@cloudsail.com
Date: 2026-09-03T16:45:00Z
Subject: Re: CloudSail SLA template — initial ask and exceptions

Team — thanks, this is helpful. CloudSail can accept the following as a path to signature: 

- Monthly credit floor: accept the tiered floor (2% / 1.25% / 0.75%) with the soft cap at 30% of monthly committed spend. Good to have the illustrative examples in the SOW.
- Batch maintenance: we agree to the 72-hour rolling notice for scheduled retrains; we will provide a list of pre-approved windows in the annex and coordinate any changes with your ops contact.
- Onboarding ramp: we accept a single 90-day ramp per environment (production only).

Please send the redlined SLA with the examples and annex language. If we get the final DocuSign link by Friday, CloudSail’s procurement will route for approval next Monday.

I’ll attach our procurement contact and the signed certificate of insurance after DocuSign.

Best,
Sarah
Sarah Park
Head of Platform Ops, CloudSail
attachments: none (will upload COI after signature)
